title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC permission reason; decree not-impede ≠ punish-impute
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: talk of imputing the father's sin belongs to his own cause—why God permitted sin's propagation—not GAR's. God was not bound to stop nature's course; pre-fall laws and begetters' desertion-earning sins blocked hindrance. Counsel/judgment toward permitting begetters their nature can somehow regard the begotten, yet is not imputation of the begetter's sin to the child. Decree not to hinder contagion ≠ decree to inflict threatened punishment.
pass_b_english: PLAC. Of the imputation of the father's sin—not to the cause the learned man is driving, but to mine, who wished to give a reason why God permitted the propagation of sin. For not only was he not bound to hinder nature's course, but that he might not hinder it, laws constituted before the fall stood in the way, and the very sins of begetters deserving desertion. But this counsel or judgment, since it regards begetters insofar as they are to be permitted their nature, can somehow be said to regard the begotten: yet it is not therefore a judgment by which the begetter's sin is imputed to the one being begotten. For one thing is a decree of not hindering sin, or the contagion or outflow of sin from parent into children; another is a decree of inflicting punishment according to the law's threat.
source_text: PLAC. De peccati patris imputatione non ad causam quam agit vir doctus, sed ad meam, qui reddere rationem volui, cur Deus propagationem peccati permiserit. Non modo enim non tenebatur impedire naturae cursum, sed ne impediret, obstabant constitutae ante lapsum leges, & ipsa generantium peccata desertionem promerentia. Hoc autem consilium seu judicium, cum spectet ad generantes eatenus sua naturae permittendos, aliquomodo ad genitos spectare dici potest: nec tamen propterea est judicium, quo generantis peccatum imputatur generando. Nam aliud est decretum de non impediendo peccato, aut peccati contagio seu dimanatione a parente in liberos, aliud decretum de irroganda secundum legis comminationem poena.

choices.choice: Permission/not-impede ≠ punish-impute of begetter's sin to child
